EDA — Stanford Ribonanza RNA Folding¶

This notebook provides a Kaggle‑ready Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) for the competition
Stanford Ribonanza RNA Folding.

It focuses on understanding the training dataset structure, sequence properties, and reactivity distributions.

Goals

  • Inspect the dataset schema (columns, dtypes, memory).
  • Assess missing values, experiment types.
  • Explore sequence properties (length, base composition).
  • Examine the distribution of base reactivity across the base position, the experiment, and the base nature (i.e., A, C, G, U).
  • Extract insights for later feature engineering and modeling.

Data Path & Plot Setup¶

This cell loads core libraries, sets the Kaggle dataset path for the Stanford RNA Folding project, prints the path for clarity, and applies consistent matplotlib styling for clean, high-resolution plots.

In [1]:
# === Standard library === 
from pathlib import Path   # filesystem paths
import io                  # buffers/files
import re                  # regular expressions

# === Third-party === 
import numpy as np                     # numerical arrays & math
import pandas as pd                    # tabular data
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt        # plotting
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
import seaborn as sns                  # statistical plots

# Dataset path (Kaggle)
DATA_PATH = Path('/kaggle/input/stanford-ribonanza-rna-folding/train_data.csv')
print('Using dataset:', DATA_PATH)  # Display active dataset path

# Plot style defaults
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (8, 4.5)
plt.rcParams['axes.grid'] = True
plt.rcParams['axes.titlesize'] = 12
plt.rcParams['axes.labelsize'] = 11
plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 320

train = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)
print('Shape:', train.shape)
print('Columns (first 20):', list(train.columns[:20]))

# Detect key columns
col_sequence = next((c for c in ['sequence', 'seq', 'Sequence'] if c in train.columns), None)
col_exp_type = next((c for c in ['experiment_type', 'exp_type', 'condition'] if c in train.columns), None)
col_dataset = next((c for c in ['dataset_name', 'dataset', 'source'] if c in train.columns), None)
reactivity_cols = [c for c in train.columns if re.match(r'^reactivity_\d+$', str(c))]

print(f"Detected: sequence={col_sequence}, exp_type={col_exp_type}, dataset={col_dataset}")

import warnings

def seq_len(s):
    return len(s) if isinstance(s, str) else np.nan

# Common axis styling
def style_axes(ax, title, xlabel, ylabel):
    ax.set_title(title, color="white", pad=6)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, color="white", labelpad=6)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, color="white", labelpad=6)
    ax.tick_params(colors="white", length=3, width=1, pad=3)

    # keep only left + bottom spines
    for spine in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color("white")
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("white")

if col_sequence:
    # === Compute lengths === 
    lengths = train[col_sequence].astype("object").map(seq_len)

    # Sequence length distribution (NO stroke)
    plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
    ax = sns.histplot(
        x=lengths,
        bins=30,
        stat="count",
        alpha=0.65,
        element="bars",      # <-- bars instead of step (removes outline)
        linewidth=0,         # <-- no stroke line
        edgecolor=None       # <-- no edge color
    )
    style_axes(ax, "Sequence Length Distribution", "Sequence length", "Count")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("Sequence_Length.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()

    # Global base composition 
    SAMPLE_N = min(10000, len(train))
    seq_sample = train[col_sequence].dropna().astype(str).sample(SAMPLE_N, random_state=42)

    counts = {'A':0, 'C':0, 'G':0, 'U':0, 'other':0}
    for s in seq_sample:
        for ch in s:
            counts[ch if ch in counts else 'other'] += 1

    comp = pd.Series(counts)

    plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
    ax = sns.barplot(
        x=comp.index,
        y=comp.values,
        alpha=0.85,
        edgecolor=None,   # <-- remove bar stroke
        linewidth=0       # <-- ensure no outline even if seaborn tries
    )
    style_axes(ax, "Global Base Composition (Sample)", "Base", "Count")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("Base_Composition.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()

Reactivity Distribution Plot¶

Samples RNA reactivity values, builds histogram bins (central 98% range), groups by experiment type if available, and plots step-line histograms without melting the DataFrame. Ensures reproducible sampling, ignores error columns, and keeps a clean axis-focused style.

In [10]:
# Filter valid reactivity columns (exclude "*error*")
react_cols = [c for c in reactivity_cols if "error" not in str(c).lower()] if reactivity_cols else []
if not react_cols:
    raise ValueError("No reactivity columns found to plot.")

# Ensure hue (experiment type) is categorical if present
has_hue = col_exp_type in train.columns if col_exp_type is not None else False
if has_hue and not isinstance(train[col_exp_type].dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
    train[col_exp_type] = train[col_exp_type].astype("category")

# RNG for reproducible row sampling
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

# Sample rows to estimate distribution range (fast)
n = len(train)
idx = rng.choice(n, size=min(n, 100_000), replace=False)
vals = train.iloc[idx][react_cols].to_numpy(copy=False).ravel()
vals = vals[np.isfinite(vals)]

# Central 98% range bins
lo, hi = np.quantile(vals, [0.01, 0.99])
bins = np.linspace(lo, hi, 50)

# Flatten helper
flat = lambda df: df.to_numpy(copy=False).ravel()

# Count hist per experiment type (or single group)
groups = train.groupby(col_exp_type, observed=True, sort=False) if has_hue else [("all", train)]
records = []
for name, g in groups:
    v = flat(g[react_cols])
    v = v[np.isfinite(v)]
    v = v[(v >= bins[0]) & (v <= bins[-1])]
    h, _ = np.histogram(v, bins)
    for left, cnt in zip(bins[:-1], h):
        records.append({"bin_left": left, "count": int(cnt), "experiment_type": name})

counts_df = pd.DataFrame(records)

# Plot stepped histogram lines
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
ax = sns.lineplot(
    data=counts_df, x="bin_left", y="count", hue="experiment_type",
    estimator=None, drawstyle="steps-post", lw=1.4, alpha=0.95
)

ax.set_xlabel("Reactivity", color="white")
ax.set_ylabel("Count", color="white")

# Ticks + spine style (keep only bottom/left)
ax.set_title("Reactivity distribution per experiment", color="white")
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(5))
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(4))
ax.tick_params(axis="both", colors="white")

ax.spines["left"].set_color("white"); ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("white")
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False); ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)

# Legend cleanup
leg = ax.get_legend()
if leg:
    leg.set_title(None); leg.set_frame_on(False)
    for t in leg.get_texts(): t.set_color("white")
        
plt.savefig("reactivity_histo.png", bbox_inches="tight")

plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

RNA Reactivity — Base-wise Summary + Export + Plot¶

This workflow computes nucleotide-specific (A/C/G/U) reactivity statistics for each experiment condition, builds a tidy summary table, saves it to Markdown, and visualizes mean reactivity with standard error on a dark-styled grouped bar chart. It handles experiment ordering, missing data, variable sequence lengths, and uses fully vectorized operations for efficiency on large RNA datasets.

In [11]:
# === Input validation === 
# Ensure sequence column and reactivity columns exist
if col_sequence is None:
    raise ValueError("Need a sequence-like column (e.g., 'sequence') to compute Base groups.")
if not reactivity_cols:
    raise ValueError("No reactivity_* columns detected.")
exp_col = col_exp_type if col_exp_type is not None else None

# === Prepare experiment column with fixed ordering (preferred first) === 
if exp_col is None:
    train["_EXP_FALLBACK"] = "ALL"               # fallback label
    exp_col = "_EXP_FALLBACK"

exp_vals = train[exp_col].astype("string")
preferred = ["2A3", "DMS"]                       # user-preferred experiments first
cats = [p for p in preferred if p in set(exp_vals.dropna())] + \
       sorted([x for x in exp_vals.dropna().unique() if x not in preferred])
train[exp_col] = pd.Categorical(exp_vals, categories=cats, ordered=True)
exps = list(train[exp_col].cat.categories)

# === Build reactivity matrix sorted by numeric position === 
pos_nums = pd.Series(reactivity_cols).str.extract(r"reactivity_(\d+)", expand=False).astype(int)
use_cols = [reactivity_cols[i] for i in np.argsort(pos_nums)]
R = train[use_cols].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32, copy=False)
N, L = R.shape
finite_mask = np.isfinite(R)                      # valid numeric values only

# === Convert sequence column to aligned base matrix (N × L) === 
seq = train[col_sequence].astype("string").fillna("").str.upper()
try:
    arr = np.array(seq.tolist(), dtype=f"U{L}")  # fast path if all same length
    bmat = np.char.array(arr).view('U1').reshape(-1, L)
except Exception:                                # fallback if variable length
    bmat = np.full((N, L), " ", dtype="U1")
    for j in range(L):
        col = seq.str.get(j)
        if not col.isna().all():
            bmat[:, j] = col.fillna(" ").to_numpy()

bases_order = ["A", "C", "G", "U"]

# === Encode experiment groups numeric for fast indexing === 
codes = train[exp_col].cat.codes.to_numpy()
exps = list(train[exp_col].cat.categories)

# === Define function to compute boxplot-like stats quickly === 
def box_stats_np(x):
    x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
    if x.size == 0:
        return dict(median=np.nan, q1=np.nan, q3=np.nan, whislo=np.nan, whishi=np.nan,
                    mean=np.nan, std=np.nan, count=0)
    q1, med, q3 = np.quantile(x, [0.25, 0.5, 0.75])
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo, hi = q1 - 1.5 * iqr, q3 + 1.5 * iqr
    whislo = float(x[x >= lo].min()) if (x >= lo).any() else float(q1)
    whishi = float(x[x <= hi].max()) if (x <= hi).any() else float(q3)
    return dict(
        median=float(med), q1=float(q1), q3=float(q3),
        whislo=whislo, whishi=whishi,
        mean=float(x.mean()),
        std=float(x.std(ddof=1)) if x.size > 1 else np.nan,
        count=int(x.size)
    )

# === Compute stats across all experiments and bases === 
stats_rows = []
for ei, exp_name in enumerate(exps):
    emask = (codes == ei)
    R_e = R[emask]
    F_e = finite_mask[emask]
    B_e = bmat[emask]

    for base in bases_order:
        mask = F_e & (B_e == base)               # finite + matching base
        vals = R_e[mask] if mask.any() else np.array([], dtype=np.float32)
        s = box_stats_np(vals)

        stats_rows.append({
            "Experiment": exp_name, "Base": base,
            "Count": s["count"], "Mean": s["mean"], "Std": s["std"],
            "Q1": s["q1"], "Median": s["median"], "Q3": s["q3"],
            "IQR": s["q3"] - s["q1"], "Whisker Low": s["whislo"], "Whisker High": s["whishi"],
        })

# === Final DataFrame ordered nicely === 
stats_df = pd.DataFrame(stats_rows).sort_values(["Base", "Experiment"])

# Compute Standard Error
stats_df = stats_df.copy()
stats_df["SE"] = stats_df["Std"] / np.sqrt(stats_df["Count"])

# Order bases + experiments
bases_order = ["A", "C", "G", "U"]
preferred_exps = ["2A3", "DMS"]
exps_all = list(pd.unique(stats_df["Experiment"]))
exps = [e for e in preferred_exps if e in exps_all] + [e for e in exps_all if e not in preferred_exps]

# Filter + set categorical ordering for plot
stats_df = stats_df[stats_df["Base"].isin(bases_order) & stats_df["Experiment"].isin(exps)].copy()
stats_df["Base"] = pd.Categorical(stats_df["Base"], bases_order, ordered=True)
stats_df["Experiment"] = pd.Categorical(stats_df["Experiment"], exps, ordered=True)

# Dark style
plt.rcParams.update({
    "axes.facecolor": dark_col,"figure.facecolor": dark_col,
    "axes.edgecolor": "white","xtick.color": "white",
    "ytick.color": "white","text.color": "white","axes.grid": False
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
fig.patch.set_facecolor(dark_col); ax.set_facecolor(dark_col)

# Bar positions
x = np.arange(len(bases_order))
group_width = 0.7
w = group_width / max(1, len(exps))
offset = -group_width/2 + w/2

palette = ["#4C72B0", "#DD8452"] + ["#888888"] * max(0, len(exps)-2)

# Draw bars + error bars
for i, exp in enumerate(exps):
    sub = stats_df[stats_df["Experiment"] == exp].set_index("Base")
    ax.bar(x + offset + i*w,
           sub["Mean"], width=w,
           yerr=sub["SE"], capsize=4,
           label=str(exp),
           color=palette[i], edgecolor=None, ecolor="white",
           linewidth=0, error_kw=dict(lw=1.8))

# Labels/ticks
ax.set_title("Mean Reactivity ± SE by Base", color="white")
ax.set_xlabel("Base", color="white")
ax.set_ylabel("Reactivity", color="white")
ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(bases_order)
ax.tick_params(colors="white")

# Spines
for side in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("white"); ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("white")

# Legend style
leg = ax.legend(title="Experiment")
plt.setp(leg.get_title(), color="white"); plt.setp(leg.get_texts(), color="white")
leg.get_frame().set_facecolor(dark_col); leg.get_frame().set_edgecolor("white")
plt.savefig("reactivity_boxplot.png", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
